leads.work: Asking for Sitara deal tickets to be extended or created when gas flows at a meter outside a deal's dates (expired deal, missing days, no evergreen flag, gas left on 'strangers gas'), so that volume management exceptions can be cleared and settlements can pay
leads.why: Many near-identical requests from Jackie Young and Aimee Lannou to Daren Farmer, one per meter. Jackie writes 'Here I go again' and 'I hate to be a pest'. Some threads run for months (Encina meter 6725 ran March to May; the Duke meters 6757/5192 run from 1999 to June 2000), with customers calling settlements about payment. A rule for auto-extending deals, or an exception report, could take this off people's desks.

leads.work: Overriding by hand the zero volumes that MIPS (measurement) sends to POPS for meters with incomplete data; the zeros flow on into Sitara and the P&L and leave volumes sitting in UA4
leads.why: Called an 'on-going problem' at 'various bidirectional meters'. Schedulers overwrite POPS with Gas Control estimates by hand, and overnight feeds put the zeros back. Measurement said a fix was 'not a priority'. Management escalated over measurement's lack of urgency.

leads.work: Reconciling UA4 (unaccounted-for gas): a 'war room' team clearing 1999 UA4, plus the monthly checking of UA4 against pipeline balancing reports
leads.why: A team of about 10 was pulled off their normal work full time for two weeks. March UA4 was over 400,000 MMBtu. Rita Wynne hopes to 'prevent crisis modes like this'. Gas-loss and meter corrections keep changing UA4.

leads.work: Filling in monthly hours and activity-driver surveys for the Operations Pricing Model (allocating costs to commercial teams)
leads.why: Sent every month to 40+ managers, with chasers. Few people replied and managers say the process is a burden. The sender offers to take a standard report instead, which would 'eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month'.

leads.work: Entering by hand EOL trades that do not bridge into Sitara (the weekday-only 24x5 product, multi-period deals, failed deals) and watching the bridge monitor for them
leads.why: Several notices confirm that the EOL-to-Sitara bridge cannot handle multiple delivery periods. Trade Capture and Risk have to split each deal into weekly lines by hand. Building a fix is still pending a cost/benefit review.

leads.work: Forwarding producer and customer nomination changes received by email (Josey Ranch revisions, Reliant egmnom spreadsheets, Calpine, Methanol/MTBE monthly noms, Walter O&G, EOG, Lyondell, ExxonMobil) and re-keying them into the systems
leads.why: Every month several numbered revisions arrive by email or attachment and are forwarded to 4-6 people each time, then entered by hand. Structured electronic intake would cut this.

leads.work: Keying in spot wellhead purchase tickets from lists the producer-services team sends by email
leads.why: Each month Vance Taylor emails tables of counterparty, meter, volume and price, and logistics re-enters them as Sitara tickets. Some of these tickets do not flow on to MOPS.

leads.work: Sending Methanol/MTBE plant upset and status emails to a fixed list of about 17 people
leads.why: Frequent repeated updates, each one prompting nomination changes.

leads.work: Resolving price and deal disagreements with counterparties before invoices can be settled (Mitchell, the PanEnergy/Duke exchange, Midcon invoices, Williams billing HPL deals to ENA, GMT paid to the wrong company)
leads.why: Long chains of follow-ups. The PanEnergy pricing fix took April to June while Duke kept calling. Unpaid Midcon invoices total about $349K. The GMT payment went to an unrelated company. A 'massive A/R issue' is mentioned.

leads.work: Reconciling PG&E Texas / PGEV volumes and rates, and doing double scheduling and allocation on both ENA and HPL transport contracts plus a desk-to-desk deal
leads.why: Variances remained unresolved for months despite repeated emails, and manual invoice line items were being used. The meeting recap says moving the ENA transport contracts to HPL would remove duplicate scheduling and allocation, but legal had not responded.

leads.work: Setting up ENA/HPL desk-to-desk deals and cleaning up interconnect and intercompany items (Cilco storage, King Ranch, Tetco 6892, Dow 4486) before the SAP implementation
leads.why: Recurring urgent requests ('bridge will close today'), plus a list of outstanding cleanup items with deadlines that spans many people.

leads.work: Refreshing rates and volumes on the monthly transport usage tickets
leads.why: Heidi Withers updates every pipe's tickets each month by hand, and schedulers then have to re-check volumes in Position Manager.

leads.work: Building monthly volume estimates for nominations and P&L (Ami Chokshi's estimates by customer)
leads.why: A series of manual calculations (averages of earlier noms, last year's figures) sent one by one by email.

leads.work: Correcting noms where they do not match flow (over-nominated meters, check meters, non-allocatable meters) because the mismatch distorts BAV and the risk P&L
leads.why: Meter 1591 kept a nom of 1,000/day for over a year while flowing almost nothing. The same kinds of questions come up repeatedly.

leads.work: Requesting and distributing Labor Distribution reports by hand, and checking payroll charges to each RC
leads.why: Managers did not receive the reports. People who had left still showed as active. Distribution was being moved to a single person by hand.

leads.work: Reviewing monthly O&M reports, preliminary ledgers, allocation percentages and IT charge reclasses
leads.why: Monthly spreadsheets forwarded for review, one with errors in every cell. Workorders were set up wrongly so costs had to be reclassed, and IT charges were missing for months.

leads.work: Collecting vacation schedules and sending out-of-office and coverage notices
leads.why: Monthly 'submit your vacation' requests and many individual coverage emails sent to large lists.

leads.work: The performance review cycle: emailing reviewer lists because the PEP system failed, collecting feedback, and long PRC meetings
leads.why: Reviewers had to be emailed for manual entry by the helpdesk. PRC meetings ran from noon until almost midnight. The cycle repeats twice a year.

leads.work: Building the Unify/Sitara enhancement backlog with estimates of hours saved
leads.why: This is a direct list of known manual pain points in Texas operations (transport contracting, hourly transactions, imbalance worksheet, UA4 tracking). Brenda Herod also asks what reports exist to manage the work.

leads.work: Contract administration follow-ups: terminations, name corrections, chasing unsigned contracts, duplicate storage deals on one contract, counterparty changes after bridge-back
leads.why: Marlene Hilliard repeatedly chases contracts that sat with Daren for months. Deals were found sharing one contract. Changing a counterparty forces repathing in Unify.

leads.work: Writing weekend on-call activity notes and handing them over to schedulers
leads.why: A long narrative of cuts and changes written up each weekend and later revised, which schedulers then have to re-enter.

leads.work: Compiling one-off research reports from Sitara and Unify (ENA sales on HPL, HPL buy/sell, Calpine force majeure days)
leads.why: Lists were assembled by hand and checked through several rounds of email. The CPR reports that already exist were mentioned only later.

leads.work: Coordinating storage purchases and payments (Cannon Interest wire, Bammel PMA revisions)
leads.why: Several people had to coordinate entry and scheduling by hand before the deal would show in Unify for payment, and reminder emails were needed.

leads.work: Planning the customer appreciation meeting (guest lists, RSVPs)
leads.why: A recurring annual event run through spreadsheets and email deadlines.
